what_happened: The person running Athena deleted, by hand, the 10 GB writer build folder of job 20261102-061427-anxh. This job is the fix for the disk-ordering bug. The bug is that the 10 GB free-space check runs before the writer's build is removed, so a job is held on low disk because of its own regenerable build. The fix job was held by the bug it fixes. No acceptance criterion, check or finding failed. It was an environment stop, and the job stays queued with its work kept.
cause: Athena has no disk lifecycle tied to a build's own state. The free-space guard counts a regenerable build as space the job needs, and the step that removes that build comes later in the stage order. The hold only waits, and nothing reclaims the held job's own build. The fix for this gap is an ordinary queued job that needs the same disk to run. It was never made urgent, so each repeat needs a hand cleanup. This is at least the eighth in the class, and the fix job has now been caught by its own bug.
prevention: Make the free-space guard act, not just report. Before the guard fires or holds a job, it should remove regenerable builds. That includes the job's own finished writer build, builds of interrupted jobs and verify-side builds. It should re-measure free space after the removal and hold or fail only if space is still below the limit. Run this at every point a build starts or a retry starts, not only at drain start. The checks should also not need the local writer build when results come from GitHub. Rank the fix ahead of other queued work until it lands.
proposed_request: Make Athena's free-disk guard reclaim space before it holds or fails a job. When free disk is below the 10 GB limit at the checks stage, first delete regenerable build folders: the job's own finished writer build, builds left by interrupted jobs, and verify-side builds. Then measure free space again, and hold the job only if it is still below the limit. Run the same reclaim when any build or retry starts, whether or not a drain is running. Do not delete anything a running or resumable job still needs, and keep the job's work (diff, report, records). Acceptance: (1) a test where the job's own writer build is the only thing keeping free space under the limit shows the job continues to checks without a hold and the build is gone; (2) a test with free space still too low after the reclaim shows the job is held, not failed, with the message naming the measured free space; (3) a test shows a retry started outside a drain removes the earlier interrupted run's build first; (4) a test shows a build still in use by a running job is not deleted. Mark this request urgent priority.
